newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power up on cold, tight supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power up on cold, tight supply.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. climbed Wednesday on forecast of frigid weather and tight supply amid outage of a transmission line that moves power from western to southeastern New York.

The outage of the high-voltage line, operated by Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, cut capacity of the Central-East Interface by 1,000 megawatt (MW). The transfer point usually has a capacity of 2,600-2,700 MW.
The maintenance shutdown of the 345 kilovolt (KV) line, which runs between Utica and Albany, began Monday and was planned to restart late Friday.
Spot supply was further tightened with talks of reduced operation at the 1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y., market sources said.
Output from the Scriba, N.Y., unit would be halved overnight to repair of a circulation pump, sources said.
"It wouldn't matter anyway because it's in western New York," replied a New York trader when asked about the event's impact on spot prices.
Niagara Mohawk, which operates Nine Mile Point 2, declined to comment on the repair.
Eastern and southern New York utilities switched on expensive fossil-fired generation to compensate for reduced supply from western New York, marketers said.

In the eastern portion of the New York Power Pool, trading of peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday was sparse, and was notationally valued in the mid-$30 a megawatt hour (MWh) range. The assessment compared with Tuesday's $31.00-$33.00.
Hourly power today in eastern NYPP was offered as high as $37.50.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Wednesday in eastern NYPP was held steady at $19.00-$20.00.
In the western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday rose in line with higher next-day prices at the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
Western NYPP power for peak, non-firm delivery on Thursday was discussed near $22.75-$23.25, up from Tuesday's $19.00-$20.00 for Wednesday.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Thursday remained at $14.25-$14.75, a tighter range than $14.00-$15.00 Tuesday.
Spot power prices in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $35.50-$36.50, up from Tuesday's $34.00-$36.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Thursday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $19.50-$20.50, a tighter range than Tuesday's $18.00-$21.00.
Vermont Yankee Power Corp fully restored the 510 MW Vermont Yankee plant after trimming its output to 80 percent of capacity the past several days to repair a condensate pump seal leak.

Thursday's temperatures in the Northeast were predicted to peak in 20-40s Fahrenheit and bottom in the teens to 20s. A cooling trend was forecast later this week with temperatures falling two to six degrees below normal Monday.
